name: Space Radiation
what: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field and atmosphere, high-energy cosmic rays and solar storms expose astronauts to ionizing radiation.
body: NASA says radiation exposure increases cancer risk and damages the central nervous system, which can affect thinking, movement and behavior.
selfCare: Wear your personal dosimeter. During a solar particle event, NASA advises crews to shelter in an area with extra shielding.

name: Isolation and Confinement
what: Crews live in small spaces far from Earth for long periods, and behavioral responses build up in isolated, confined groups.
body: Sleep loss, circadian desynchronization and work overload can add to this strain, lowering performance and harming health.
selfCare: Watch for sleep loss and overwork. NASA is studying light therapy to help keep body clocks aligned.

name: Distance From Earth
what: The farther from Earth, the harder it is to get instructions, new supplies and medical care. Mars missions face up to 20-minute one-way communication delays.
selfCare: Plan ahead and be self-sufficient: NASA says crews must handle situations with minimal support from teams on Earth.

name: Gravity Fields
what: Crews float in weightlessness and must readjust each time they move between gravity levels, such as landing on the Moon or Mars.
body: Weightlessness can cause dizziness, bone and muscle loss, and vision problems from fluids shifting toward the head. Kidney stone risk can rise.
selfCare: Track balance and vision changes. Weight-bearing bones lose 1% to 1.5% of mineral density per month in spaceflight, so bone health matters.

name: Hostile/Closed Environments
what: A spacecraft is a closed ecosystem. Temperature, pressure, lighting, noise and microbes all shape daily life on board.
body: Microbes spread more easily between people in closed habitats. Stress hormones can rise and the immune system can change, possibly raising allergy or illness risk.
